memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “The righteous shall live by faith.” — Romans 1:17

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
There is a beautiful yet dangerous word that Satan softly whispers into the ears of believers:  “Just adjust.” ,“Make a small compromise.” But righteousness never allows even a little compromise.
Joseph was called righteous, not because his life was easy, but because his heart refused to bend. In Potiphar’s house, temptation came dressed as opportunity. Pleasure was offered. Position was hinted at. Secrecy was promised. Yet Joseph did not adjust. He did not negotiate. He did not even pause to think. He fled. Joseph chose to lose his garment, but he refused to lose his purity.

Even today, Satan uses the same strategy. He calls compromise “balance,” cowardice “wisdom,” and surrender “intelligence.” Potiphar’s wife offered comfort and flattering words. But that path would have led Joseph into sin, bondage, and broken peace. Joseph’s prison looked like defeat, but it actually made him inwardly free.
Compromise chains the soul. Righteousness, even in chains, keeps a man free. In every generation, the righteous face greater testing.
For Joseph, it was sexual purity.
For some, it is money. For others, fame, position, or the silence that cooperates with evil. Joseph did not pray long prayers in the moment of temptation he ran.
And here is the eternal truth Joseph teaches us:
It is far better to suffer for righteousness than to succeed through compromise. God may allow a season of prison, but the righteous who refuse compromise will surely be delivered and honored in the end.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “A man who is right with God has no need to compromise with the world.” — Leonard Ravenhill

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me the courage to flee from compromise and the grace to stand firm in righteousness. I choose righteousness over adjustment. I will not compromise. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: Stand and fight to glorify God.
Heaven honors the man or woman who refuses to bend.

recommended_book.label: Recommended Book
recommended_book.title: “Why Revival Tarries”
recommended_book.author: Leonard Ravenhill
recommended_book.quote: Ravenhill reminds us that revival is delayed not because of ignorance, but because of compromise. God is still searching for men and women who will stand upright in a bending generation those who will not trade holiness for convenience.
